messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Elevated 5xx spike detected in control-plane (auth mesh). 5xx rate ~3.1% across eu-west and ap-southeast, surge starting 2025-11-03T14:02Z. Auto-paged to #incidents and paging group oncall. Metrics: https://metrics.redwood.example/alerts/5567890123 :alert:

sana: i'm on it. seeing a pile of 502s for /v1/org/lookup and /auth/verify. SLOs are degraded for token-exchange routes. Anyone else seeing trace spikes? can we confirm customer-facing impact? :eyes:

support-ops: we have customer reports of login failures in EU, handful of enterprise users. CS triage says ~10 tickets opened in last 10m, mostly timeouts and 502s from app logs.

raj: looking at traces now — spans show upstream to billing-service and org-db returning 502/connection reset. The auth-proxy sidecar shows connection pool exhaustion errors and repeated TCP resets. bulk of errors originate from the auth mesh sidecar (sidecar-proxy v2.3.1).

morgan: repro locally on a small load test: when auth-proxy sees >120rps to billing service we hit 'connection pool exhausted' and requests return 502. KV cache miss rate jumped ~x6 which amplified load to billing. logs from a proxy pod:```
[2025-11-03T14:05:12Z] WARN connection_pool.cpp:89 - connection pool exhausted, pending=312
[2025-11-03T14:05:13Z] ERROR http_client.cpp:213 - connect() failed: ECONNRESET
[2025-11-03T14:05:14Z] ERROR handler.cpp:142 - upstream returned 502
```

ida: proposed mitigations (short-term):
1) Temporarily route org-lookup requests to cached variant (org-lookup-cache) via routing rule — reduces load on billing.
2) Increase sidecar connection pool limits from 100 -> 400 (hot config roll, no full restart).
3) Apply tenant-level ingress rate-limit to 50 rps for bulk tenants that are spiking.
4) If pool change doesn't hold, scale billing-service replicas by +2 and enable circuit-breaker fallback to 200ms.
Please call the playbook: /run playbooks/controlplane-auth-throttle (need approval)

sana: i'm rolling the routing rule for org-lookup -> org-lookup-cache now (canary to eu-west-1, 10% traffic). Deploy bot: `deploy-bot: started rollout 5567890135 - route:org-lookup->org-lookup-cache (canary 10% eu-west-1)`

incident-bot: update: paging escalation to oncall level 2 at 2025-11-03T14:08Z.

raj: applying quick config patch to sidecar pool limit. patch pushed to configmap sidecar-proxy-config v20251103-02, hot-reload initiated on proxies in eu-west. Command run:
```bash
kubectl set -n controlplane configmap sidecar-proxy-config --from-literal=conn_pool=400 && kubectl rollout restart ds/sidecar-proxy -n controlplane --grace-period=30
```

morgan: increased pool looks to be taking effect — connection_pool exhausted logs dropping. KV cache miss rate still high but org-lookup canary is showing 80% reduction in calls to billing. 5xx rate in eu-west dropped from 3.1% -> 0.9% in last 5m.

support-ops: customer-facing update: posting to status.redwood.example: "We are investigating elevated errors impacting login and some API requests in EU/APAC. Mitigations underway; no data loss suspected."

ida: rolling tenant-level ingress throttle for top 10 noisy tenants in eu-west (temporary). throttle set to 50 rps.

incident-bot: note: oncall handoff scheduled at 2025-11-03T15:00Z. current assignee sana handing to night oncall ida.

sana: summary of immediate mitigation results:
- canary routing to org-lookup-cache (10%->100%) rolled successfully at 14:17Z
- sidecar conn pool increased -> running at 400
- ingress throttle applied to noisy tenants
- billing-service scaled +2 replicas as precaution
Outcome: overall 5xx reduced to baseline ~0.2% in eu-west. ap-southeast still showing a ~0.6% residual spike, likely due to lagged cache warm.

morgan: digging apac issues — looks like one regional cache node in ap-southeast was OOM-killed yesterday and didn't fully warm; org-lookup fallback still hitting upstream. restarting cache node should help. issuing `kubectl rollout restart sts/org-cache -n controlplane -l region=ap-southeast`

raj: done, restarted cache pod; after warm-up ap-southeast 5xx down to 0.15%.

support-ops: CS confirms reduction in new tickets, existing ones updated. No escalations to executive comms needed.

ida: quick customer impact note for postmortem: peak impact window 14:02Z-14:20Z, peak 5xx ~3.1% across control-plane auth mesh. Estimated error volume ~1200 reqs/min at peak, affecting token exchange and org-lookup; several enterprise customers saw transient login failures. No persisted data loss, retries succeeded for many requests; some client-side fallout.

morgan: root cause hypothesis: combination of cache warm failure in apac + sidecar conn pool configured too low for sudden delta in miss-rate; this cascaded to billing service and caused connection exhaustion -> 502. Contributing factors: alert thresholds didn't account for KV cache stampedes, and routing lacked a cache-fast fallback before hitting billing.

ida: next steps / action items (assigned):
- [ida] follow up with runtime team to add autoscaling for org-cache and add readiness check so OOM-killed nodes don't take long to warm (ticket INFRA-1422).
- [morgan] add canary and test for sidecar conn pool changes; add config guardrails (RUNTIME-995).
- [raj] tune alerting: separate cache-miss-stampede alert and lower noise (SRE-1803).
- [sana] customer comms follow-up and support notes update.

sana: handing off to ida for night coverage. please keep thread updated if anything regresses. thanks all. :pray:

incident-bot: incident closed for active paging at 2025-11-03T14:45Z — mitigations in place, residual monitoring active. Created incident ticket INC-20251103-06 for postmortem and action tracking.
